appearance.organs.panicle.note: The panicle's layout, the model's choice after FNA (volume 24), as search results quote it (the page was not read): contracted, 1 or 2 branches a node, erect to slightly spreading. Drawn as 8 branches in pairs close to the axis, each with about 5 spikelets. Colours by eye.

traits.note: FNA's account of the species (volume 24), as search results quote it (the page itself was not read): inflorescences (7)8 to 20(25) cm, loosely to densely contracted, with 1 or 2 branches a node, the branches erect to slightly spreading; spikelets 9 to 13.5 mm, with 4 to 6 florets; glumes shorter than the upper florets, the lower (2)2.5 to 5 mm, the upper 4 to 6.2 mm; lemmas 5 to 7(8.2) mm; awns (2)3 to 5 mm, at the tip.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a dense, fine-leaved bunchgrass with thread-like, blue-green blades in a round tuft and narrow panicles. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 0.7 m tall at 4 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: blue-green blades; straw-coloured panicles.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.life_span.note: Hitchcock (p. 58, 76-77) puts F. idahoensis, in which F. roemeri was then included, in section Eufestuca, plants perennial.

traits.rhizome_habit.note: Hitchcock (p. 76, no. 33, F. idahoensis in the broad sense, which then held F. roemeri): culms usually densely tufted in large bunches, no rhizomes named.

traits.clonal.note: Hitchcock (p. 76, no. 33, F. idahoensis in the broad sense): a dense bunchgrass with no rhizomes or stolons named.

traits.culm_length_m.note: GrassBase's entry for F. roemeri (as search results quote it; the page itself was not read): culms erect, (35-)50-90(-100) cm long; Hitchcock's F. idahoensis in the broad sense is 30-100 cm.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: GrassBase's entry for F. roemeri (as search results quote it; the page itself was not read): leaf-blades conduplicate (folded), 0.5-1(-1.2) mm wide.

traits.inflorescence_length_m.note: GrassBase's entry for F. roemeri (as search results quote it; the page itself was not read): panicle open or contracted, (7-)8-20(-25) cm long; Hitchcock's F. idahoensis in the broad sense is 10-20 cm.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (Festuca no. 23, F. idahoensis, which then included the coastal plants now F. roemeri): blades numerous, mostly basal, 15-30 cm long, sometimes shorter. Read as F. idahoensis in the broad sense.

traits.flowering_months.note: Abrams vol. 1 (Festuca no. 23, F. idahoensis in the broad sense): flowers May-July in open woods and rocky slopes.
